The 8% support price increase is independently documented by a reseller notice at https://corp.ba-net.co.jp/news/20260625_1 — and it is the FOURTH consecutive 8% year, so it is a run-rate, not a new lift, which is why support revenue grows 1.1%: the installed base is attriting into cloud.

The ORCL reaction is sourced separately from the price series: https://en.cryptonomist.ch/2026/09/15/oracle-stock-falls-4-7-despite-30-revenue-surge-charts-stay-bearish/ (2026-09-15) and https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/10/oracle-orcl-q1-earnings-report-2027.html for the parent's Q1 FY2027 figures. Note this finding shares NO document with finding 1 — one is the consensus/mix arithmetic, the other is the tape and the positioning — but they are the same trade and I have sized the total below their sum accordingly.

The H1 base it is measured against comes from a different source: FY2026/2 H1 actuals of 営業収益 ¥111,549m (+8.0%), 営業利益 ¥5,858m (+1.9%), 経常利益 ¥5,905m (+2.5%) — https://diamond-rm.net/flash_news/523550/. The Q1 figures and the 21.8%-vs-24.7% progress comparison come from IFIS 株予報, https://kabuyoho.ifis.co.jp/index.php?action=tp1&bcode=2742&sa=report, and from https://nikkeiyosoku.com/stock/2742/ (Q1 営業収益 ¥57,876m +7.2%, 営業利益 ¥2,728m -10.5%, 経常 ¥2,747m -10.2%). NOTE: this finding shares its arithmetic with the guidance finding below — the guidance finding is sized only as the incremental cost of a formal revision, not as a second reading of the same H1 number.

The wage decision is corroborated independently at https://taxlabor.com/kagawa-minimum-wage/ (Kagawa ¥1,092 from 2026-10-01, +¥56). The H2 arithmetic rests on the same H1 estimate as finding 1 — declared, not independent — and the FY guide itself is sourced separately to https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZRST0501415Q6A410C2000000/ (2026-04-10).

Lopia's own operator confirms the openings and the cadence from a different source: OIC Group press release 2026-05-07 for 新市店 opening 2026-05-15 (https://oicgroup.co.jp/docs/release/2026-05-07-%E5%82%99%E5%BE%8C%E3%82%A8%E3%83%AA%E3%82%A2%E5%88%9D%E3%80%81%E5%BA%83%E5%B3%B6%E7%9C%8C%E5%86%852%E5%8F%B7%E5%BA%97%E3%81%A8%E3%81%AA%E3%82%8B%E3%80%8C%E3%83%AD%E3%83%94%E3%82%A2%20%E6%96%B0%E5%B8%82%E5%BA%97%E3%80%8D%E3%81%8C5%E6%9C%8815%E6%97%A5%E3%82%AA%E3%83%BC%E3%83%97%E3%83%B3.pdf), and Halows' own 2026-04-09 renovation of its 戸手店 in the same 新市町 (https://www.ryutsuu.biz/store/s040941.html) is a defensive capital action in the same postcode five weeks before Lopia arrived. What does NOT support a Lopia reading: Halows' June existing-store -1.3% is explained by an industry-wide event, not by Lopia — the three supermarket associations reported the first YoY decline in 40 months for June 2026 on rice base effects and rice price deflation (https://shokuhin.net/153929/2026/07/23/ryutu/kouri/), and that broad series beats the narrow inference, so I have deliberately not built any part of this finding on the June number.

The suppression of new openings and the DOE-3%/payout-35% return policy that the plan rests on come from a different document, the VISION2028 mid-term plan coverage at https://finance.logmi.jp/articles/384354 ; the Q1 revenue and cost figures come from Nikkei's 2026-06-22 report at https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUF19A610Z10C26A6000000/ . Pointing the OTHER way, and recorded here rather than buried: direct competitor DAIWA CYCLE (5888) released H1 (Feb-Jul 2026) results and an August sales flash on 2026-09-14 reporting record half-year sales and operating profit (https://www.daiwa-cycle.co.jp/ir/library/presentation/), after a Q1 of revenue 69.6億 +12.3% and OP 6.56億 +7.3%, so the category through July was not weak and Asahi's problem is company-specific cost and share, not collapsing demand. June: https://www.ryutsuu.biz/sales/s070844.html (2026-07-08). August: https://www.ryutsuu.biz/sales/s091142.html (2026-09-11). The Yahoo 掲示板 thread of 2026-09-24 discusses it (https://finance.yahoo.co.jp/quote/8227.T/forum) but quotes different figures (112.9% same-store), so it is not load-bearing. The only figure used is the Wealth Advisor one.

The plan assumptions (既存店 99.1% H1, GM 58.2% FY, H1 OP ¥2,200m) come from a different document, the 2026-07-07 決算説明会資料 (https://www.honeys.co.jp/ir/library/detail/378?attach=true&fld=file&browserview=true). The retail margin build is from kabutan 信用残 (https://kabutan.jp/stock/kabuka?code=2792&ashi=shin). Each is one input to a single calculation, not separate confirmation of the conclusion.

Cross-checked against last year's backlog table (FY2025/5 決算短信, https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20250709/140120250708509794.pdf: backlog -2.8% at 2025-05-31, followed by Q1 sales +8.6%) and the Q4 sales from kabutan's 3-month table (https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=7921). Those are two readings from the company's own documents, so they count once. The one different-source datum points the other way: Pronexus (7893) Q1 Apr-Jun 2026 (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260731/140120260730503996.pdf) shows sales +5.3%, mostly from M&A, and OP +0.4%. 招集通知 revenue fell (about 90 fewer listed companies, electronic provision cutting print pages) and English translation orders fell. That drag is already netted into the +1.0; without it I would size about +1.5. A primary company document beats an industry proxy, so the peer read cuts the size but does not flip the sign.

The progress-rate arithmetic comes from a different document: the Q1 supplement https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260626/140120260626581136.pdf (plan ratios, Enchō -793 OP bridge) and last year's H1 supplement https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20250926/140120250926563086.pdf (Q2 FY26 OP 11,158 on existing-store -4.3%, showing DCM can hold Q2 profit on falling comps via cost control). That is why the low end sits at -2.5.

The opposing crowd is the retail margin long of 1,629,100 shares (8.8%), which rose in the week to 09-25 (kabutan 週次信用残: https://kabutan.jp/stock/kabuka?code=2354&ashi=shin). Partly independent: MLIT 建築着工統計 for July 2026 shows the housing investment estimate +19.5% YoY (https://www.mlit.go.jp/report/press/joho04_hh_001390.html). The terms are corroborated by independent secondary coverage of the same document (https://discoveryalert.com/asx-stock-news/mining/wc8-wildcat-resources-tabba-tabba-a60m-placement/), but that is not independent evidence of the reaction. The 25 Sep close is from https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/WC8.AX?range=3mo&interval=1d.

Separate primary documents show the same Q3 commitment and the earlier slip: the 15 Jan 2026 Strategic Outlook ('Project Delivery Plan is expected to be completed in Q2 2026', https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260115/pdf/06v8tjg65s0v3h.pdf); the 1 Jul 2026 update ('will release a Project Delivery Plan during the current quarter', https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260701/pdf/0716t81bbw8xg5.pdf); the June-quarter 5B (Plan, mining contract award and 'first drawdown under the SFA is expected to occur in Q3 2026', https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260730/pdf/0726xmx6fybcx7.pdf). The 14 Sep 2026 drilling release puts further assays in Q4 2026 (https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260914/pdf/0741n40vnkfhgy.pdf). That raises the odds the reserve update waits for them, and it is why the central estimate sits near zero.

It is the same holder and the same filing series, so it is not independent evidence. The tape (Yahoo PEN.AX: 20d run-up -13.56%, 5d -8.93%) is consistent but does not prove it.
